Grace —

Quick summary from our side: BrightLeaf is approaching our contract renewal window (end of April) and we want to align on a path that keeps latency predictable for our freshness-sensitive features while managing cost. We saw a ~28% token spend increase in February (attached CSV) from a model change on our side and a small uptick in tail latency (p99 from 420ms to ~610ms on a few heavy request patterns).

High level asks:
- Can Redwood offer a short bridge (1-2 months) with burst credits while we finalize a larger commit?
- Can you share a latency breakdown by model variant (we suspect our switch to the larger Llama family variant is affecting runtime)?
- We want a proposed committed tier that avoids frequent headroom failures — need backlog to 3M tokens/month minimum with predictable pricing.

I've attached the usage CSV and a sample p99 trace; Evan (cc) can share a list of affected endpoints. Would appreciate a 30–45 minute sync this week.

Thanks,
Maria Lopez

Subject: Fwd: Q1 usage + renewal planning (triage suggestions + quantization note)

Forwarding Maria's thread — initial thoughts from Eng Ops / Solutions:

- Root cause candidate: model variant shift + an increase in average sequence length due to a recent feature (context window growth). That combination increases KV-cache pressure and results in higher p99 during some bursts.
- Quick mitigation: enable per-route prefix caching (reduces repeat attention compute), and evaluate int8 quantization for the serving variant — often reduces per-token cost by ~30–45% while preserving quality for classification/summary workloads.
- For the bridge: we can scope a 2-month program with defined burst credits and guardrails (auto-fallback to a smaller variant if sustained p99 > 900ms for 15 mins).

I attached a short runbook for the p99 investigation and a draft latency mitigation plan with estimated delta on token economics.

Action items for the sync: we should bring a short scoreboard: current run-rate, 90/95/99 latency, expected uplift with quantization, and a recommended committed tier.

— Soojin
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
